title: API testing with REST Assured and load testing with JMeter

videos.script: Lesson 19 tested the bookshop in pieces. The service, with a mock. The repository, against a real PostgreSQL. {{pieces}} None of those tests sent a request. No JSON was written, no token was checked, and no status code was read. {{gap}} A client sees only what crosses the wire, so this lesson tests the wire. {{wire}} The test starts the whole application on a random port, and REST Assured talks to it over HTTP. Given this request, when it is sent, then the answer looks like this. {{given}} You test a book, the problem detail for a book that does not exist, and an order placed with a real token. {{token}} Then the question changes. How many answers a second, and how long do the slowest ones take? {{load}} JMeter sends twenty readers at the catalogue at once, and counts. {{jmeter}} The numbers come with a warning. On one computer, the load and the application share the same processors. Part of what you measure is the computer. {{limits}}
